killings.evidence: laust horninu í höfuð honum svo að drykkurinn slóst niður á Brand ... keyrði öxi í höfuð honum og vó hann (ch. 11)
killings.settled_after: yes (ch. 11: þeir tóku fébætur)

killings.evidence: Ótryggur lagði spjóti til Eyjólfs ... En er Eyjólfur sá það þá lagði hann Ótrygg í gegnum með spjóti (ch. 27)
killings.settled_after: yes (ch. 30–33: settlement at Hegranessþing; 'frá því er allir voru sáttir', ch. 33)
killings.note: A pitched fight at Veisa. Ótryggur was the son-in-law of Þorkell hákur, earlier killed by Guðmundur ríki, and attacked Eyjólfur first.

killings.evidence: undi mjög illa við það að eigi komu mannhefndir eftir víg Koðráns bróður hans ... báru þegar vopn á hann og vógu hann (ch. 33)
killings.settled_after: yes (ch. 33: kom þar að manngjöld skyldi lúka og galst það fé allt)
killings.note: Koðrán was killed by Hallur Ótryggsson (ch. 27). Þórarinn was a brother of Þorvarður, the leader of the opposing side, not of the actual killer. The killing broke an existing settlement.

killings.evidence: Steingrímur gaf Hróa hundrað silfurs til þess að drepa Hánef (ch. 5); Þóroddur harðjaxl vó Helga bróður Hróa (ch. 6)
killings.settled_after: yes (ch. 6: Sú var gerð Áskels að vígin skulu á standast)
killings.note: An ambush fight over Hánefur (the sheep-theft case). Hrói was hired by Steingrímur.

killings.evidence: Vémundur skaut snærisspjóti og kom á skjaldarsporð Steins ... Þorvaldur son Galta úr Arnarnesi féll í naustdyrunum fyrir Steini (ch. 13)
killings.settled_after: yes (ch. 13: víg Þorvalds skal vera til sýknu Helga Þorbjarnarsonar en Galta skal bæta hundraði silfurs)
killings.note: Vémundur's party attacked Steinn (Steingrímur's brother-in-law) after the killing of Herjólfur; Steinn defended himself.

killings.evidence: Þórir ... leyndist þar þá er hann sá hversu Steingrími hafði farist ... hjó hann þegar til Áskels goða (ch. 16)
killings.settled_after: yes (ch. 16: vígin Áskels og Steingríms skyldu á standast; Þórir skyldi fara utan)
killings.note: Steingrímur fell through the ice or was speared by Vémundur during the fight. Áskell was Vémundur's kinsman and leader of that party. No revenge word is used.

killings.evidence: Hávarður ... fór á fund Skútu vinar síns og sagði honum um ferðir Glúms ... segja nú Skútu að Hávarður mun eigi bera oftar njósnina (ch. 24)
killings.settled_after: unclear (ch. 24 settlement covers the Eyjólfur and Bjarni case)
killings.note: Hávarður was killed as Skúta's informer while Már was serving a summons.

killings.evidence: báðu hann ráðagerðar til að drepa Skútu Áskelsson því að hann hafði drepið föður þeirra og bróður ... ráðið þeim ráð til hefnda eftir föður sinn (ch. 30)
killings.settled_after: yes (ch. 30: Þórður illugi sekur ... utan þrjá vetur ... voru nú sáttir að kalla)
killings.note: Skúta had killed Þórir (the killer of Skúta's father Áskell, KL193). That killing is not in the input.

killings.feud_name: Valla-Ljótur & Svarfdælir vs Halli's kin & Guðmundur ríki
killings.evidence: "Það ætla eg við lög varða að vinna á Mikaelsmessu ... og mun eg stefna þér um helgibrigði." ... Halli tók við fénu (ch. 3); hjó Ljótur Halla banahögg (ch. 4)
killings.settled_after: yes (ch. 5: hundrað silfurs var goldið fyrir víg Halla)
killings.note: Halli extorted money from Ljótur through a lawsuit, egged on by Guðmundur ríki.

killings.feud_name: Valla-Ljótur & Svarfdælir vs Halli's kin & Guðmundur ríki
killings.evidence: "muntu nú mega hefna bróður þíns" ... "Eg ætla nú að fara og hefna Þorvarðar frænda míns." (ch. 6)
killings.settled_after: yes (ch. 8–9: Guðmundur's vígsmál settled, payments made)
killings.note: Þorvarður was killed in breach of a truce by Hrólfur gípa, brother of Halli and Böðvar (ch. 5). Bessi is Hrólfur's nephew.

killings.evidence: gerðu til handa sér akurinn ... Glúmur leit yfir akurinn og mælti: "Eigi brást hann Vitaðsgjafi enn." (ch. 7–8)
killings.settled_after: yes (ch. 9: Þorkell sættist á mál og seldi Glúmi landið)
killings.note: Over the field Vitazgjafi and Sigmundur's false theft charge against Ástríður's thralls.

killings.evidence: fann það til saka að hann hefði fleira talað við Þórdísi konu hans en skaplegt væri ... Þá höggur Arngrímur til hans í höfuðið (ch. 20–21)
killings.settled_after: yes (ch. 23: bæta skyldi víg Steinólfs)
killings.note: Steinólfur was Glúmur's kinsman. The killing led to the battle at Hrísateigur.

killings.evidence: eg vark at þar og vák at þar og rauðk at þar odd og egg er Þorvaldur krókur fékk bana (ch. 25)
killings.settled_after: yes (ch. 26: Glúmur galt Þverárland hálft Katli syni Þorvalds króks í föðurbætur ... varð héraðssekur)
killings.note: Killed in the battle at Hrísateigur (ch. 22–23). Þorvaldur krókur had been with Arngrímur at Steinólfur's killing. Glúmur's ambiguous oath comes in ch. 25.

killings.evidence: tóku þeir af Klængi rekaldið nauðgum ... Klængur hleypur að honum og veitti honum banasár (ch. 27)
killings.settled_after: unclear (ch. 27: Þórarinn and Þórður prosecute; the confiscation court fails)
killings.note: A beached-whale dispute. Klængur was Glúmur's kinsman and Glúmur backed him against the Eyfirðingar.

killings.evidence: Þorkell og Héðinn vógu Þorgils föður Brodd-Helga (ch. 1)
killings.settled_after: unclear (ch. 1)
killings.note: Genealogical mention only; no cause or aftermath is given. Two killers of one victim.

killings.evidence: Þorkell og Héðinn vógu Þorgils föður Brodd-Helga (ch. 1)
killings.settled_after: unclear (ch. 1)
killings.note: Genealogical mention only; no cause or aftermath is given. Two killers of one victim.

killings.evidence: Þá Svart og Skíða skildi á um beitingar og lauk því svo að Svartur vó Skíða. En Brodd-Helgi mælti eftir vígið og gerði Svart sekan. (ch. 2)
killings.settled_after: no (ch. 2: Svartur outlawed)
killings.note: Brodd-Helgi later kills the outlaw Svartur (not in input), after sheep thefts.

killings.evidence: Tjörvi hinn mikli skyldi ... vera í brottu ... (ch. 14); Hann strýkur eftir honum og rekur í gegnum hann spjótið ... Hún segir: "Betra er það en ekki." (ch. 14)
killings.settled_after: no (ch. 14: Geitir gaf ekki Bjarna skuld fyrir þetta)
killings.note: Tjörvi rode with Geitir when Brodd-Helgi was killed (ch. 13). The settlement had banished him from the district. Text damaged (lacuna) around ch. 13–14.

killings.evidence: "Nei," sagði hún, "Bjarni mun hefna þín." (ch. 13); Bjarni hjó þá í höfuð Geiti (ch. 14)
killings.settled_after: yes (ch. 19: gerði hann hundrað silfurs fyrir víg Geitis)
killings.note: This breaks the settlement for Brodd-Helgi (ch. 14). Bjarni was goaded by his stepmother Þorgerður; the manuscript is damaged at that point. The revenge word comes from the prophecy in ch. 13.

feuds.summary: Þorbjörn kills Atli Ásmundarson and Grettir avenges his brother by killing Þorbjörn. It is only summarised in a genealogy.

A slander killing, lawsuits, an adultery killing and the killing of Hallsteinn set Helgi and Grímur Droplaugarson against Helgi Ásbjarnarson. Helgi Ásbjarnarson kills Helgi; Grímur avenges him and is outlawed.
After King Haraldur kills Þórólfur Kveldúlfsson, Kveldúlfur and Skalla-Grímur avenge him on the king's men and emigrate to Iceland.

Egill kills Bárður and Gunnhildur has a man of Þórólfur's killed. Later the inheritance dispute with Berg-Önundur leads to Egill's outlawry and his killing of Rögnvaldur Eiríksson. It continues until Egill buys his head at York.
A battle abroad in which Egill kills Aðils jarl right after Aðils's men kill Þórólfur.
Egill is ambushed on a tax-collecting mission and kills his attackers.

feuds.feud_name: Lambi vs Ketill gufa's runaway thralls
feuds.summary: Ketill gufa's runaway thralls burn Þórður Lambason inside his house. His son Lambi hunts them down and kills them.

feuds.feud_name: Þorsteinn Egilsson vs Steinar (grazing at Stakksmýri)
feuds.summary: Steinar's thralls graze cattle on Þorsteinn's land and Þorsteinn kills two of them. Egill arbitrates the lawsuit.

feuds.feud_name: Eiríkur rauði vs Eyjólfur saur's kin
feuds.summary: Eyjólfur saur kills Eiríkur's thralls and Eiríkur kills him and Hólmgöngu-Hrafn. Eiríkur is driven out of Haukadalur.
Jöður kills Hávar in a quarrel over a horse, and Hávar's 15-year-old son Þorgeir avenges him. A settlement follows.
Urged on by Sigurfljóð, the foster-brothers kill a robber father and son. Sigurfljóð buys them peace from Vermundur.
Þorgeir kills Þorgils Mársson over a whale and later his kinsman Gautur. Gautur's kinsman Þórarinn ofsi and Þorgrímur trölli kill Þorgeir, and Þormóður avenges his sworn brother in Greenland.
Þorgeir kills a man who did not answer him (Flateyjarbók text).
Þormóður kills the thrall Loðinn after being dragged across the floor. Skúfur settles it with sjálfdæmi.

feuds.feud_name: Björn the berserk vs Þorkell skerauki's sons
feuds.summary: Björn kills Ari in a holmgang for his wife and land, and Gísli the elder kills Björn.

feuds.feud_name: Gísli vs Þorgrímur & Börkur (killing of Vésteinn)
feuds.summary: Vésteinn's secret killing is avenged by Gísli on Þorgrímur, and later by Vésteinn's sons on Þorkell. Gísli is outlawed and finally killed.

feuds.feud_name: Þórir & Múli vs Helgi of Hjallar (grazing)
feuds.summary: A grazing dispute leads to Gunnar killing Þórarinn ákafi. Revenge ambushes by Helgi's sons and by Helgi end with their deaths, and the matter is settled.
Whale and land disputes lead to ambushes and a battle at Langeyri. Steinólfur and Hallur burn Ketilbjörn and Þórir takes revenge; Hallur dies and his son accepts a settlement.
Rivalry over Helga ends in a duel in Norway. Gunnlaugur kills Hrafn's kinsmen and both rivals die.

feuds.feud_name: Hörður & the Hólmverjar vs the district men
feuds.summary: The outlaw band on Geirshólmur is lured ashore and Hörður is killed by Þorsteinn gullknappur. Revenge is later sought on the slayers.
Styr kills Þórhalli over an unmarked sheep and mocks the son with a lamb as compensation. Gestur avenges his father and escapes abroad.
Barði's revenge for his brother Hallur ends in a battle on the heath, followed by a settlement.
Hrafnkell kills his shepherd Einar for riding Freyfaxi. Sámur wins the lawsuit and humiliates Hrafnkell, who later regains power.
Þórólfur kills Ingjaldur's brother Hallur over a catch of fish. Vigdís hides him and he escapes abroad.
Hrútur kills Eldgrímur, who was taking Þorleikur's horses by force.
Rivalry over Guðrún and a string of insults end with Bolli killing Kjartan. Revenge killings follow on both sides until a final settlement.
Auðgísl, backed by Snorri goði, kills Þorgils over a seized goðorð and is killed immediately.
A killing told in another saga and only mentioned here.

feuds.feud_name: Bolli Bollason vs Þórólfur stertimaður & the Hjaltasons
feuds.summary: Þórólfur kills a boy over a dead bull. Bolli has him outlawed and kills him, and a settlement follows (ch. 89).
Brandur kills Hárekur after being struck with a drinking horn. Compensation is paid.
A paternity case leads to a fight at Veisa where Ótryggur and Koðrán die. Eyjólfur breaks the settlement to avenge Koðrán, and compensation is then paid.
The Hánefur case and Vémundur's provocations lead to repeated killings. Steingrímur and Áskell die at the river ice and Skúta avenges Áskell. Þórir's sons finally kill Skúta and a settlement follows.
Hostility between Skúta and Glúmur; Glúmur's son Már kills Skúta's informer Hávarður.

feuds.feud_name: Valla-Ljótur & Svarfdælir vs Halli's kin & Guðmundur ríki
feuds.summary: Ljótur kills Halli after Halli extorts money from him, and Hrólfur gípa kills Þorvarður in breach of a truce. Björn avenges Þorvarður on Halli's kin, and Ljótur settles with Guðmundur.

It starts with Glúmur's killing of Sigmundur over Vitazgjafi. Arngrímur's killing of Steinólfur leads to the battle at Hrísateigur; Glúmur's false oath costs him Þverá and he is banished from the district.
Mentioned only in the genealogy.
Svartur kills Skíði over grazing and is outlawed. He then preys on Hof's sheep and the young Brodd-Helgi kills him.
Geitir kills Brodd-Helgi. Bjarni kills Tjörvi and, goaded by his stepmother, Geitir, then settles with Geitir's son Þorkell.
